title: Jude and the Static
premise: Ada Dunmore smuggles memories through orbital customs above Meridian, a dying colony the war has written off. When the long-lost deep-space ship Vesper returns with its crew aged backward into children who remember their own deaths, Ada is hired to move the one memory that proves the war's opening attack was staged by both governments. Pursued by customs agents and the colony's desperate militia, she must choose between selling the memory to the highest bidder or broadcasting it free as the jump window closes — and she broadcasts it, ending the war but burning her own criminal empire, finding in the Vesper's crew the family she never had.
about_author: Bram Fairweather is the pen name of a former radio technician who spent six years on remote relay stations before turning to fiction. They write about people who keep signals alive when no one is listening.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: POV Ada. A routine smuggling run through orbital customs introduces her world: dying Meridian, black-market memory chips, and her handler Okafor's quiet warnings that the war is closing in. She carries a widow's last memory of her husband for free — establishing her code. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: The Ship That Came Back
chapters.summary: POV Ada. The Vesper docks unannounced after eleven years; its crew are children wearing adult scars of memory. Customs seals the ship, and a dying engineer begs Ada to smuggle out one chip before the military confiscates everything. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as she realizes what she's holding.

chapters.title: Children Who Remember Dying
chapters.summary: POV Ada, hiding in the underdeck slums. She plays fragments of the chip and discovers it contains proof the war's first strike was ordered from inside both governments. The child-crew member Sef, aged backward to nine, recognizes her voice from ship recordings. Emotional beat: reluctant connection — Sef refuses to leave her side.

chapters.title: Customs House Fire
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Agents raid Okafor's network hunting the chip; Okafor burns his own warehouse to cover her escape and disappears. Ada learns the price on her head exceeds anything she's ever earned. Emotional beat: guilt — her code of carrying others' griefs has finally cost someone real.

chapters.title: The Militia's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Meridian's militia leader, Reyes, offers protection in exchange for the chip — she wants leverage to force evacuation ships for the colony. Ada stalls, realizing every faction wants the truth weaponized. Sef teaches her the Vesper's old crew songs. Emotional beat: found family forming in the cracks of a siege.

chapters.title: What the Widow Knew
chapters.summary: POV Ada. The widow from chapter one resurfaces: her husband was a customs auditor whose final memory corroborates the chip. His death wasn't accidental. Ada assembles the full chain of evidence across three sources. Emotional beat: resolve hardening — this is no longer cargo, it's testimony.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Relay
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Reyes sells them out to the military to guarantee her colony's evacuation. Sef is taken; Ada barely escapes with the chip, wounded, into the derelict relay stations where Bram's radio past echoes in the setting. Emotional beat: betrayal's cold arithmetic — everyone trades someone to survive.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: POV Ada. The window for broadcasting system-wide opens in thirty-six hours and closes for a year. Ada infiltrates the orbital array with help from an unlikely ally: a customs agent who lost family in the staged strike. Emotional beat: terror and clarity — one transmission, no second chances.

chapters.title: Static
chapters.summary: POV Ada, climax. Military jamming floods the band as she fights through the array's defenses; Sef, escaped and stowed aboard, opens a door only the Vesper's crew could know. Ada broadcasts the full testimony — the war's founding lie — to every ship and colony at once. Emotional beat: sacrifice and release as her smuggling empire, her anonymity, all of it burns away.

chapters.title: Signal, Received
chapters.summary: POV Ada, resolution. Ceasefires ripple outward; tribunals form; Meridian gets its evacuation ships. Ada, now a wanted-and-celebrated ghost, chooses to stay with the Vesper's child-crew as they rebuild. Sef calls her family without ceremony. Emotional beat: quiet belonging — survival was the price, but not the point.
